mainEntity.name: What is brand identity development?

acceptedAnswer.text: Brand identity development is the process of building a complete identity system for a business. It covers both the strategic foundation (positioning, narrative, audience) and the visual and verbal system (logo, colour, typography, visual language, tone of voice). The output is a documented system that determines how the company is seen, heard, and remembered across every surface.

mainEntity.name: What is included in a brand identity system?

acceptedAnswer.text: A complete brand identity system typically includes: a brand strategy document (positioning, narrative, audience definition, brand architecture), a logo suite and visual mark, a typography system, a colour palette, a visual language (illustration style, photography direction, motion principles where relevant), a verbal identity and tone of voice, packaging design where the brand has a physical product, and a documented set of brand guidelines that govern how the system is applied.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between brand strategy and brand identity?

acceptedAnswer.text: Brand strategy is the thinking layer: positioning, narrative, audience, and the role the brand plays in the world. Brand identity is the expression layer: logo, colour, type, visual language, and verbal voice that carry the strategy into form. A brand identity built on weak strategy looks fine and fails to mean anything. A strategy without a strong identity stays trapped in a deck. The best brand identity development projects build them together.

mainEntity.name: How much does brand identity development cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Brand identity development costs vary widely with scope, complexity, and the seniority of the studio. At Izart, engagements typically start from $5,000 and scale with the depth of strategy required, the breadth of the visual system, and the stage of the brand. The right investment depends on the long-term commercial ambition of the business. We share a tailored estimate once the brief is clear.

mainEntity.name: How is Izart's approach to brand identity any different?

acceptedAnswer.text: Izart treats brand identity as infrastructure rather than decoration. The studio is built around talent density rather than headcount, so every decision of consequence is made by senior practitioners who carry strategy and craft in the same head. Each engagement reads the culture the brand is entering before it makes a mark, and builds the identity as a system designed to hold meaning at scale across every surface and every stage of the brand's growth.

mainEntity.name: When should a startup invest in a full brand identity?

acceptedAnswer.text: A startup should invest in a full brand identity once the business model is validated, the audience is identified, and the company is ready to scale beyond the founder's personal network. Investing too early can lock the brand into a position the company outgrows. Investing too late means the brand is already living in the market with inconsistencies that compound. The right moment is after product-market fit and before significant scaling.

mainEntity.name: Does Izart offer brand strategy as part of brand identity development?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every brand identity development engagement at Izart includes the brand strategy layer: positioning, narrative, audience definition, and the strategic foundation that the visual identity is built on. Strategy and identity are handled inside the same body of work, by the same team, so the thinking arrives in the form rather than getting lost between handoffs.

mainEntity.name: Where is Izart based?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our office is based in Delhi. Our entire team works from the same office to maintain a consistency of output across different streams of operations. We work with clients from all parts of the world with projects completed for ventures across 50+ geographies. Typical engagements run remotely, however we can be on-ground where the work calls for it.

mainEntity.name: What services does Izart Studio Offer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Izart Studio offers branding & strategy, UI UX design, web design & development, e-commerce, and campaign planning services.

mainEntity.name: How does Izart work with brands on an ongoing basis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Izart works with brands through custodianship arrangements that vary with the pace at which the internal team takes ownership. Many relationships sit at twelve to eighteen months, with some continuing for longer.

mainEntity.name: How long does an engagement run?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engagement lengths depend on the scope. A full brand build, from strategy through identity, digital, and launch, typically runs three to six months. Custodianship, where it follows, runs longer and varies with the pace at which the internal team takes ownership. Many relationships sit at twelve to eighteen months. Some have continued for longer.

mainEntity.name: What kind of ventures does Izart Studio work with?

acceptedAnswer.text: Izart Studio works with ventures across 50+ geographies worldwide, from early-stage startups to established brands.

mainEntity.name: How does Izart charge?

acceptedAnswer.text: We work on retainers and fixed-scope project fees, depending on the shape of the engagement. We are explicit about scope at the start, and we structure the work in phases so each one delivers something complete rather than partial. Fees are sized to the work, the timeline, and the seniority of the team running it.

mainEntity.name: Do you work for equity?

acceptedAnswer.text: In select cases, yes. Where the founder profile aligns with our internal investment thesis, we deploy creative capital in exchange for equity rather than fees, in whole or in part. These arrangements are reviewed against the same criteria we would apply to any early-stage bet: the strength of the founder, the shape of the category, and the long-term commercial logic of the brand we would build alongside them.

mainEntity.name: What is included in website design and development services?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full website design and development engagement typically covers: discovery and audit, sitemap and information architecture, wireframing, visual design of every key template, front-end and back-end build on the chosen tech stack, content load, cross-browser QA, performance and SEO optimisation, and deployment. The handover includes a documented design system and the access required for the internal team to maintain and extend the site.

mainEntity.name: How long does a website design and development project take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard website design and development project typically runs six to eight weeks from kickoff to launch, depending on the page count, the complexity of the interactions, and the chosen tech stack. Larger marketing sites or stores with custom integrations can take ten to fourteen weeks. The timeline is set against the scope, never against an industry default.

mainEntity.name: Which tech stack should I choose: Webflow, Framer, Shopify, or custom?

acceptedAnswer.text: The right tech stack depends on what the site needs to do. Webflow suits marketing-first sites that the internal team will edit post-launch. Framer fits animation-heavy, interaction-rich brand sites with shorter content scope. Shopify is the default for D2C and e-commerce brands. Custom builds are reserved for sites with complex application logic, deep integrations, or scale requirements beyond what no-code platforms support. We recommend a stack only after understanding the brand's roadmap.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between website design and website development?

acceptedAnswer.text: Website design is the work of designing the site: visual layout, interaction logic, content templates, brand expression on screen. Website development is the work of building the designed site into a functioning product on the chosen tech stack. The best projects treat them as one body of work rather than two handed-off phases, because the design and the build inform each other at every step.

mainEntity.name: How much does a website project cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: At Izart, website design and development engagements typically start from $5,000 and scale with the scope of the site, the complexity of the interactions, and the tech stack required to support the brand's roadmap. Each project is scoped against the brief, so the investment reflects what the work actually requires rather than a fixed package price. We share specifics once we understand what is being built.

mainEntity.name: Does Izart Studio work with brands that already have an existing website?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A common engagement is rebuilding a site for a brand that has outgrown its current one: better information architecture, stronger conversion logic, modernised tech stack, deeper integration with the brand identity that has evolved since the previous build. Discovery for these projects includes an audit of the existing site so the new build absorbs what is working and replaces what is holding the brand back.

mainEntity.name: Do you provide post-launch support and maintenance?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Post-launch support is available either as ongoing custodianship, where Izart continues to design and build new pages, run marketing creative, and govern the brand on the site over time, or as staffing and training, where we hire and train the internal team that will run the site daily, with monthly check-ins for six months afterwards. Both shapes are detailed on the Custodianship service page.

mainEntity.name: How does Izart's website design and development differ from a freelancer or template-based site?

acceptedAnswer.text: A freelancer or template-based site is built fast and looks fine at launch. It tends to break down as the brand evolves and traffic scales. Izart approaches a website as a system, designed and engineered together by senior practitioners, on a tech stack chosen against the brand's needs, with documentation that allows the internal team to extend cleanly. The difference shows up two years in, when the cheap site has been rebuilt and the well-built site is still compounding.
